paragraphs: Planning under partial observability means choosing actions without knowing the exact state of the world. A POMDP represents this uncertainty through a belief: a probability distribution over possible states. Large problems make exact belief updates and consideration of every possible observation difficult, so planning methods approximate both using samples.

AdaOPS improves this sampling-based approach in two connected ways. It uses an adaptive particle filter to improve the sampled representation of a belief. It also combines branches of the planning search associated with similar observations. Combining branches balances estimation bias and variance, addressing how the planner uses its limited samples as well as how it represents uncertainty.

The theoretical result is conditional: under assumptions described as mild, sufficient planning time gives a high probability of finding a policy within a specified tolerance of optimality. Experiments on several challenging POMDP domains report better performance than the state of the art in every tested domain. Together, these findings support adaptive belief approximation and observation grouping as useful components of online planning.
neurips-2021-adaptive-online-packing-gui.tldr: AdaOPS improves planning under state uncertainty through adaptive belief sampling and merging similar observation branches.

paragraphs: Offline policy evaluation asks how useful a decision-making policy would be using only an existing dataset. Much of its theory assumes that the chosen model can represent, or closely approximate, the relevant environment. This paper examines the less understood situation where a linear model does not adequately represent that environment.

The authors analyze an existing estimator, the linear direct method, rather than introducing a new policy-learning procedure. Their main result characterizes its evaluation error asymptotically, meaning in the limit as the amount of data grows. The characterization is exact in that limit and has a doubly robust form, giving a structured account of error when model realizability cannot be assumed.

The authors then use this analysis to establish nonparametric consistency for tile-coding estimators under assumptions they describe as quite mild. Consistency means that estimation approaches the correct value as data grows under those conditions. The contribution therefore links an error analysis for misspecified linear evaluation to a positive convergence result for a particular family of estimators.
neurips-2021-asymptotically-exact-error-.tldr: The paper characterizes the asymptotic error of linear offline policy evaluation under misspecification and establishes consistency for tile-coding estimators.

paragraphs: Conditional image generation must combine a source of variation with information that guides the output. The paper identifies a mismatch in existing polynomial neural networks: their success at generating images from noise relies on single-variable expansions, while conditional generation involves both noise and a conditioning input. Simply having a successful unconditional generator does not resolve how those inputs should interact.

CoPE addresses this by expanding two input variables together. Its formulation captures relationships within each input and across the two inputs, making their interaction part of the polynomial representation. The framework can also be extended to accept an arbitrary number of input variables, broadening the kinds of conditioning information it can accommodate.

The evaluation covers eight datasets and five task categories: class-conditioned generation, inverse problems, edges-to-image translation, image-to-image translation, and attribute-guided generation. The reported evidence suggests usefulness across diverse conditional tasks. The central contribution is a general way to represent multiple interacting inputs in polynomial generators, with empirical support across these different settings.
neurips-2021-conditional-generation-usin.tldr: CoPE extends polynomial neural networks to conditional generation by explicitly modeling relationships within and between multiple inputs.

paragraphs: A reinforcement learning agent that operates over a long lifetime needs to keep learning while retaining useful knowledge. That creates competing demands: limited model capacity and computation, avoiding the loss of earlier skills, and using previous experience to learn new tasks more effectively. The authors argue that these trade-offs have received uneven attention, with too much emphasis on forgetting.

Continual World shifts attention toward forward transfer: whether earlier learning helps with later tasks. It provides a benchmark of realistic, meaningfully varied robotic tasks built on Meta-World. This makes the usefulness of accumulated knowledge a central evaluation concern alongside the preservation of previously learned behavior.

The paper evaluates existing continual learning methods in depth, identifying limitations and challenges specific to reinforcement learning. The benchmark is intended to offer a meaningful challenge at modest computational cost. Its contribution is both an evaluation resource and a proposed change in emphasis: successful continual learning should include improved learning on new tasks, not just retained performance on old ones.
neurips-2021-continual-world-a-robotic-b.tldr: Continual World benchmarks continual robotic learning with an emphasis on whether past experience improves learning on new tasks.

paragraphs: The paper studies constrained sampling through mirror-Langevin diffusion, a continuous-time process that must be turned into discrete steps for computation. The authors propose a new discretization and prove its convergence. The central issue is whether this implementable sequence of steps approaches the desired probability distribution under useful assumptions.

Their analysis combines relative convexity, relative smoothness, and self-concordance, concepts originating in convex optimization. It also introduces an optimal-transport result extending displacement convexity of entropy. These ingredients provide a way to analyze the interaction between the target distribution and the mirror map used by the sampling method.

Compared with prior work, the guarantees require substantially weaker assumptions on both the mirror map and the target distribution. They also establish that sampling bias vanishes as the step size approaches zero. For log-concave distributions supported on compact sets, the authors report significantly improved theoretical guarantees. The contribution concerns both the discretization and the mathematical conditions under which constrained sampling can be justified.
neurips-2021-efficient-constrained-sampl.tldr: A new mirror-Langevin discretization offers convergence under weaker assumptions and bias that vanishes as the step size shrinks.

paragraphs: Text-guided video temporal grounding locates the time interval corresponding to an event described in words. This paper combines several visual signals because ordinary color images, although informative about appearance, can be distracted by background clutter. The aim is to identify the relevant event using complementary evidence about what appears, what moves, and how the scene is structured.

The framework uses RGB images for appearance, optical flow for large motion, and depth maps for scene structure and shape-related object cues. A transformer-based dynamic fusion mechanism models interactions among these three modalities. Additional self-supervised learning strengthens each modality's representations across videos, supporting the subsequent combination of their information.

Experiments on Charades-STA and ActivityNet Captions show favorable performance against state-of-the-art approaches. The stated findings support combining appearance, motion, and structure for temporal localization, with learned interactions among those signals. The method's contribution is therefore not just adding visual inputs, but providing mechanisms for learning both within individual modalities and across them.
neurips-2021-end-to-end-multi-modal-vide.tldr: The method locates text-described video events by dynamically combining appearance, motion, and depth information.

paragraphs: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo samples from probability distributions whose normalizing constant need not be known. Its practical implementation commonly uses a leapfrog integrator, and performance can depend strongly on the chosen mass matrix. This paper develops a gradient-based method for adapting that matrix to improve how the sampler moves through the target distribution.

The adaptation encourages proposals that are likely to be accepted while exploring dimensions jointly. Its objective maximizes an approximation to proposal entropy, emphasizing the spread of proposed moves. This differs from earlier adaptation methods based on expected squared jumping distance. The aim is to improve exploration while retaining the acceptance behavior needed for useful sampling.

The paper illustrates that using multiple gradients in an HMC proposal can be beneficial relative to a single gradient step in Metropolis-adjusted Langevin proposals. Empirical results suggest that the adaptation can outperform different HMC variants by matching the mass matrix to the target's geometry and providing some control over integration time. These are reported empirical advantages, rather than a universal performance guarantee.
neurips-2021-entropy-based-adaptive-hami.tldr: An entropy-based adaptation method tunes HMC's mass matrix to encourage accepted proposals that explore dimensions jointly.

paragraphs: Federated learning lets clients train a shared model without sharing their underlying data. This paper asks how to prepare an initial model that a later group of clients can adapt within only a few communication rounds. The difficulty is that the group's eventual task may be unknown when that starting model is constructed.

The authors use meta-learning to train the initialization for the adaptation process itself. Training episodes imitate a prescribed number, R, of federated learning rounds followed by inference. This arrangement makes the short federated training process part of what the initialization is optimized to support. The meta-learning stage can itself be carried out through federated learning among willing participants.

Experiments report good generalization across client groups and large performance improvements over baselines using other pretraining methods at the same overall communication and computation resources. The intended benefit is rapid adaptation, including to possibly unseen tasks. The evidence supports preparing an initialization around the downstream collaboration procedure rather than judging its usefulness only before that procedure begins.
neurips-2021-few-round-learning-for-fede.tldr: The method meta-learns an initialization designed to help new client groups train effective federated models in only a few rounds.

paragraphs: Neural architecture search can be expensive when assessing candidates requires fully training many networks. Performance predictors reduce that burden by estimating how well architectures will ultimately perform. This paper addresses the difficulty of comparing those predictors when evaluation measures differ and methods are designed for different initialization and query-time budgets.

The study analyzes 31 techniques spanning learning-curve extrapolation, weight sharing, supervised prediction, and zero-cost proxies. It evaluates correlation-based and ranking-based measures across multiple settings. It also examines whether predictors actually speed up search frameworks that use them, connecting predictive quality to their intended role in architecture selection.

The findings provide recommendations that depend on the operating setting rather than identifying a single universally preferred predictor. They also show that combining certain predictor families can improve predictive power. A released library collects the 31 methods. The contribution is a broad comparative foundation for choosing and combining predictors while considering both prediction behavior and the computational constraints of the search process.
neurips-2021-how-powerful-are-performanc.tldr: A study of 31 architecture-performance predictors identifies useful choices for different settings and benefits from combining certain families.

paragraphs: Goal-conditioned hierarchical reinforcement learning uses a high-level policy to propose subgoals. For complex, long-horizon tasks, the possible subgoals can form a large action space, making exploration inefficient. HIGL addresses this by guiding the high-level policy with landmarks: states selected as promising places to explore.

Landmark selection uses two complementary criteria. One favors coverage of the states already visited, while the other favors novelty measured through state prediction error. The method then organizes landmarks into a graph and selects the first landmark along a shortest path. Training encourages the high-level policy to generate a subgoal toward that selected landmark.

This structure reduces the high-level action space and gives exploration an intermediate direction. Coverage and novelty influence which states become landmarks, while graph paths influence which landmark guides the next subgoal. Experiments across a variety of control tasks report improvements over prior methods, attributed to more efficient landmark-guided exploration. The findings support this combination of state selection and subgoal guidance in the evaluated tasks.
neurips-2021-landmark-guided-subgoal-gen.tldr: HIGL improves hierarchical exploration by guiding subgoals toward landmarks selected for coverage and novelty.

paragraphs: In stochastic shortest-path learning, an agent repeatedly tries to reach a goal at minimum expected total cost without initially knowing action costs or environment dynamics. The paper studies regret over K episodes: the extra cost incurred while learning compared with optimal behavior. Its main result identifies the worst-case achievable rate in terms of problem size and optimal-policy cost.

The upper bound scales, up to logarithmic factors, as the square root of (B² + B) times the number of states, actions, and episodes. Here B bounds the optimal policy's expected cost from any state. For B at least one, the result matches an existing lower bound up to logarithmic factors and improves the previous upper bound by a square-root-of-state-count factor. For smaller B, the paper proves a matching lower bound.

The algorithm reduces shortest-path learning to finite-horizon decision problems. A supporting algorithm makes the leading regret term depend polynomially on optimal expected cost but only logarithmically on the horizon. This connects the learning guarantee more closely to cost while controlling horizon dependence.
neurips-2021-minimax-regret-for-stochast.tldr: A reduction to finite-horizon learning yields stochastic shortest-path regret bounds matching lower bounds up to logarithmic factors.

paragraphs: Imitation learning from observations gives a learner the states an expert visited without revealing the expert's actions. This removes information that standard imitation learning can use directly. MobILE tackles this setting with a model-based framework that balances following the expert's observed behavior against exploring the environment to resolve uncertainty.

The method combines distribution-matching imitation learning with optimism in the face of uncertainty. Matching distributions supplies the imitation objective, while optimism provides a way to incorporate exploration. A unified theoretical analysis establishes strong performance guarantees for classes of decision-process dynamics satisfying specified, previously studied notions of complexity.

The paper also establishes that observation-only imitation is strictly harder than standard imitation learning. A connection to a multi-armed bandit problem shows that exploration is necessary for efficient solutions in this setting. Simulations on benchmark OpenAI Gym tasks support MobILE's effectiveness. Together, the results explain why observation-only demonstrations require an exploration strategy and provide a framework with both conditional theoretical guarantees and experimental support.
neurips-2021-mobile-model-based-imitatio.tldr: MobILE combines optimistic exploration with distribution matching to learn from expert state sequences without expert actions.

paragraphs: Online optimization asks a learner to make repeated decisions while loss functions change over time. This paper studies that problem when decisions lie on a Riemannian manifold, a space with its own geometry. The objective is to control regret while accounting for geometric structure beyond the usual Euclidean setting.

The authors analyze Riemannian online gradient descent on Hadamard manifolds for geodesically convex and strongly geodesically convex losses. These conditions express convexity along the space's geodesics. They also analyze a Riemannian bandit algorithm for geodesically convex losses on Hadamard homogeneous manifolds, giving a separate result for a setting with more restricted feedback and additional geometric structure.

The upper bounds track the effects of time horizon, curvature, and dimension. A constructed online optimization problem supplies a universal lower bound on achievable regret. The authors report that the resulting bounds match corresponding Euclidean results, and numerical experiments support the theory. The findings extend familiar online-learning guarantees to the specified curved spaces while making their geometric dependencies explicit.
neurips-2021-no-regret-online-learning-o.tldr: The paper establishes regret guarantees for gradient and bandit learning on specified Riemannian manifolds that match corresponding Euclidean results.

paragraphs: Path integration means updating an estimate of position using self-motion. The paper studies a grid-cell representation in which a two-dimensional position becomes a higher-dimensional vector, and movement transforms that vector. The question is what properties these transformations need for coherent position updates and well-behaved representation errors.

The analysis identifies two conditions with different roles. A group-representation condition is necessary for path integration. An isotropic-scaling condition ensures a locally conformal embedding, so local errors in the representation translate conformally into position errors. The authors then examine linear transformations, describing their algebraic and geometric structure through a matrix Lie group of rotations.

The paper also explores a connection between isotropic scaling and a special class of hexagonal grid patterns. An optimization-based approach learns hexagonal patterns with properties similar to rodent grid cells, and the resulting model performs accurate long-distance path integration. These results connect mathematical conditions on movement representations to learned spatial patterns and navigation behavior without establishing that the brain necessarily uses this model.
neurips-2021-on-path-integration-of-grid.tldr: The paper connects group-structured motion updates and isotropic scaling to grid-cell representations and learned hexagonal patterns.

paragraphs: Expert demonstrations can guide reinforcement learning through a behavioral reference policy. KL regularization encourages the learning policy to remain close to that reference, an approach that has improved sample efficiency in challenging physical tasks. This paper examines how the reference policy itself can create problematic online training dynamics.

The authors show empirically that commonly chosen behavioral policy classes can produce slow, unstable, and suboptimal learning. They examine consequences for both sample efficiency and the performance of the resulting online policy. The finding makes the representation of demonstrated behavior a consequential part of the learning procedure, rather than merely a preliminary way to summarize expert data.

The proposed remedy is to use nonparametric behavioral reference policies. The paper reports that these can resolve the identified pathology and enable KL-regularized reinforcement learning to significantly outperform state-of-the-art approaches on varied locomotion and dexterous hand manipulation tasks. The result supports changing how the reference is represented while retaining demonstration-based regularization as a useful source of guidance.
neurips-2021-on-pathologies-in-kl-regula.tldr: Common demonstration-derived reference policies can destabilize KL-regularized learning, and nonparametric references can remedy the identified pathology.

paragraphs: Changing decisions can incur costs beyond the loss associated with each decision itself, such as wear from changing server status. This paper studies online convex optimization with a budget on total switching cost. The learner must achieve low regret while respecting that cumulative restriction on how much its decisions change.

The lower bounds reveal two regimes. When switching budget S is at least on the order of the square root of horizon T, the regret lower bound is of square-root-T order. For smaller budgets, it is of order the smaller of T/S and T. The proof uses an adaptive adversary whose losses respond to the learner's accumulated switching cost. A simple gradient-based algorithm achieves minimax-optimal regret.

Stronger curvature improves the achievable guarantees. For strongly convex losses, logarithmic regret is attainable with a switching budget of logarithmic order. Smaller budgets give an upper bound of order the minimum of T/exp(S) + S and T. These results quantify how available switching and loss curvature jointly affect learning performance.
neurips-2021-online-convex-optimization-.tldr: The paper characterizes optimal regret under a total switching budget and shows improved guarantees for strongly convex losses.

paragraphs: Rules offer an understandable way to express knowledge, derive further conclusions, and communicate with other reasoning systems. The paper argues that existing rule induction is constrained in two ways: knowledge-base methods stay within a fixed knowledge base, while supervised language-model methods inherit patterns from their annotated training rules.

The authors formulate open rule induction as extracting open rules from knowledge contained in language models. Their Orion system mines such rules automatically without supervision from annotated rules. The intended change is to exploit the expressive capacity of language models without requiring the discovered rules to follow the templates supplied by a rule-annotation dataset.

Experiments assess both the quality and quantity of the induced rules. When used for downstream relation extraction, the automatically obtained rules outperform manually annotated rules in the reported evaluation. This provides evidence that the mined rules can be useful beyond the induction process itself. The result supports language models as a source for discovering usable rules, rather than only generating variations of supervised examples.
neurips-2021-open-rule-induction-fd49583.tldr: Orion mines open rules from language models without annotated-rule supervision and demonstrates their usefulness for relation extraction.

paragraphs: This paper investigates whether parametrized quantum computations can serve as useful policies in reinforcement learning. It proposes a hybrid quantum-classical model using very few qubits. The work addresses two distinct questions: whether such a model can learn standard benchmark tasks and whether quantum policies can offer a provable advantage on particular learning problems.

For practical trainability, the authors show that their model can be trained effectively in several standard benchmark environments. This establishes that the proposed quantum-classical policy representation can support learning beyond specially constructed theoretical examples. The reported benchmark result concerns solving those environments; the abstract does not equate it with a demonstrated quantum advantage on them.

Separately, the authors demonstrate and formally prove that parametrized quantum circuits can solve certain learning tasks that are intractable for classical models, including state-of-the-art deep neural networks. This separation depends on the widely believed classical hardness of the discrete logarithm problem. The theoretical advantage is therefore conditional and task-specific, accompanying the distinct evidence of benchmark trainability.
neurips-2021-parametrized-quantum-polici.tldr: Quantum-classical policies solve standard benchmarks and offer a conditional, provable advantage on certain learning tasks.

paragraphs: Contextual bandits adapt decisions as a study proceeds, potentially improving participants' outcomes while learning useful policies. That adaptation complicates later statistical analysis. Standard estimators may lose asymptotic normality, so familiar confidence intervals can fail to cover the true quantity at their intended rate.

The paper introduces the Contextual Adaptive Doubly Robust estimator, or CADR, for policy value. Its central construction stabilizes estimation under contextual, adaptive data collection. The technical challenge is to estimate conditional standard deviations in a way that is both adaptive and consistent. This addresses difficulties that arise when observations depend on context as well as previous learning.

The authors establish asymptotic normality for CADR, providing a basis for confidence intervals after adaptive collection. Numerical experiments using 57 OpenML datasets report that CADR-based intervals uniquely achieve correct coverage among the evaluated approaches. The contribution connects adaptive decision-making with credible post-study policy evaluation: collecting data to improve decisions need not preclude useful uncertainty estimates when the estimator accounts for the collection process.
neurips-2021-post-contextual-bandit-infe.tldr: CADR stabilizes policy-value estimation from contextual bandit data to support asymptotically normal inference and valid confidence intervals.

paragraphs: Compressing generative adversarial networks can reduce the computation and memory needed for deployment on resource-constrained devices. This paper argues that concentrating on the generator overlooks the discriminator's role during training. GCC coordinates both components so that a lightweight generator can be trained with a suitably adjusted adversarial partner.

Its discriminator selectively activates convolutional channels according to local capacity and global coordination constraints. These constraints help maintain equilibrium with the smaller generator and avoid mode collapse. The original generator and discriminator are also trained from scratch as teacher models, progressively refining the pruned generator and selectively activated discriminator.

An online collaborative distillation procedure transfers intermediate features from both teacher components to improve the lightweight generator. Experiments across several GAN generation tasks support the scheme's effectiveness and generalization. In image translation, the reported result is an 80% reduction in computational cost while retaining comparable performance. The findings emphasize that compression quality can depend on coordinating adversarial training and teacher guidance, not solely on reducing generator size.
neurips-2021-revisiting-discriminator-in.tldr: GCC coordinates generator compression, discriminator capacity, and teacher distillation, reporting 80% lower computation with comparable image-translation performance.

paragraphs: Stylized dialogue generation aims to produce a response in a requested style while remaining connected to its conversational context. The paper considers the absence of paired contexts and target-style responses. Existing approaches create synthetic training pairs through back translation, but the authors argue that they insufficiently model generated contexts and interactions among the available text domains.

Multi-pass dual learning builds mappings among three domains: contexts, target-style responses, and responses in an intermediate style. The framework must reconstruct the context, and reconstruction error supplies a training signal. This uses relationships among all three domains to guide learning when direct target-style training pairs are unavailable.

The method also introduces discriminators to assess whether a synthetic sequence fits its intended domain. Their assessments determine how much weight the corresponding synthetic data receives during training. Evaluations report significant improvements over previous baselines. The contribution combines reconstruction-based learning with explicit assessment of generated training data, addressing both how synthetic examples are produced and how strongly they influence the dialogue model.
neurips-2021-stylized-dialogue-generatio.tldr: Multi-pass dual learning improves stylized dialogue by reconstructing contexts across text domains and weighting synthetic examples by domain fit.

paragraphs: The Topographic VAE connects organized latent representations with equivariance: representations changing predictably when inputs transform. It introduces a way to train deep generative models whose latent variables have a topographic organization. On MNIST, the model organizes activations around salient properties including digit class, width, and style.

The authors extend this organization over time using temporal coherence. For sequences of transformed inputs, this encourages predefined transformation operators in latent space. The resulting feature groups, called capsules, learn approximately equivariant behavior directly from sequences. The claim is about encouraged, approximate correspondence between input and representation transformations.

The model achieves higher likelihood on test sequences undergoing corresponding transformations. The authors also measure equivariance by checking approximate commutativity: whether transforming an input and then encoding it agrees with the corresponding transformation of its encoding. Demonstrations include complex transformations, expanding the capabilities described for existing group-equivariant networks. The findings show how temporal organization can help a generative model learn structured responses to transformations without supervised equivariance targets.
neurips-2021-topographic-vaes-learn-equi.tldr: Topographic VAEs use spatial and temporal latent organization to learn feature groups that transform approximately equivariantly.

paragraphs: In online learning with feedback graphs, a graph over actions specifies what feedback the learner receives. This paper develops one algorithm with regret guarantees for adversarial losses, stochastic losses, and stochastic losses affected by adversarial corruption. The objective is to retain protection against difficult sequences while benefiting from more regular data.

The bounds depend on the graph's clique covering number, denoted theta, and the number of rounds T. Adversarial regret is of order square root of theta times T. Stochastic regret is theta times a polylogarithmic function of T. With C adversarial corruptions, the guarantee adds a square-root-of-theta-times-C term to the stochastic bound, explicitly accounting for the corruption level.

The algorithm uses Follow-the-Regularized-Leader with a regularizer combining Tsallis and Shannon entropy components through a product structure. Establishing convexity and controlling the inverse Hessian of this regularizer are key technical contributions. These properties support the simultaneous guarantees, connecting a carefully designed optimization penalty to adaptation across different loss environments.
neurips-2021-towards-best-of-all-worlds-.tldr: A combined-entropy regularizer gives one feedback-graph learning algorithm regret guarantees for adversarial, stochastic, and corrupted stochastic losses.

paragraphs: Earlier proofs of recurrent neural networks' Turing completeness allowed neurons to store values with unbounded precision. This paper removes that precision assumption by giving a bounded-precision network a dynamically growing memory module. Its focus is the computational capacity of the resulting system rather than a training procedure for discovering programs.

The memory consists of fixed-precision neurons. It recruits neurons when more storage is needed and releases them when stored information becomes irrelevant. The construction therefore accommodates increasing memory requirements through growth in the memory module. The distinction matters: bounded precision does not mean the entire computing system has a fixed amount of memory.

The authors prove that a 54-neuron bounded-precision RNN equipped with growing memory modules can simulate a Universal Turing Machine. Simulation time is linear in the simulated machine's running time and independent of memory size. They extend the result to other stack-augmented RNNs and revisit both bounded- and unbounded-precision cases. The result strengthens the theoretical foundation for recurrent computation with finite-precision components and expandable storage.
neurips-2021-turing-completeness-of-boun.tldr: A 54-neuron bounded-precision RNN with dynamically growing memory can simulate a Universal Turing Machine with linear-time overhead.

paragraphs: Vision transformers model long-range relationships through self-attention, but their treatment of images as token sequences does not inherently encode local visual structure or variation in object scale. ViTAE incorporates convolutional structure to provide these inductive biases directly. The motivation is to help the model represent useful image properties that would otherwise need to be learned implicitly.

Spatial pyramid reduction modules use convolutions with different dilation rates to downsample images and produce tokens containing context at multiple scales. Within each transformer layer, a convolution block runs alongside multi-head self-attention. Their features are fused before entering the feed-forward network, allowing local feature learning and global relationship modeling to work together.

Experiments on ImageNet and downstream tasks report superiority over the baseline transformer and concurrent approaches. The architecture's contribution is the combination of scale-oriented token construction with local processing throughout the transformer. The findings support incorporating convolution-derived biases into attention models so that representations can use both nearby visual structure and relationships across distant parts of an image.
neurips-2021-vitae-vision-transformer-ad.tldr: ViTAE combines multiscale convolutions and self-attention to give vision transformers built-in biases for locality and scale variation.
